column12: note

column1: # --- u06.l01 Todos los días (regular present). Also new here, row in core.tsv: comida

column5: to have dinner; to have supper
column12: La cena is a light evening meal.
La cocina is the kitchen.
Hago: I do. ¿Qué haces?: What are you doing?
No to: escucho música.
The everyday Mexican word for a chat.

column5: to come back; to go back
column12: More common in Mexico than volver.

column1: # --- u06.l02 Empiezo a las nueve (stem-changing verbs)

column12: Pienso que sí: I think so.
Jugar futbol: to play soccer.
Mexico writes futbol and stresses the last syllable.
To ask a question is preguntar.
¿Cómo se dice...?: How do you say...?

column1: # --- u06.l03 ¿Qué hora es? (time, days). tarde (noun) must stay above tarde#late: the first is the default link

column12: ¿Qué hora es?: What time is it?
En la mañana: in the morning. Mañana alone: tomorrow.
Llegar tarde: to be late.
Days take no capital: el lunes, los lunes.

column1: # --- u06.l04 Me levanto temprano (reflexive verbs, routine)

column12: Me baño usually means I take a shower.
Lavarse los dientes: to brush your teeth.

column5: to get ready; to dress up

column12: Salgo de casa: I leave home.
Me voy: I'm off. Ya nos vamos: we're leaving now.

column5: to go to bed; to lie down

column12: Más tarde: later.

column1: # --- supporting (no lesson introduces these; usable from Unit 6 on)

column12: Una vez: once. A veces: sometimes. Otra vez: again.
Y media: half past.
No accent. ¿Cuándo? asks when.
Antes de: before.
Después de: after.
(Yo) desayuno also means I have breakfast.
(Ella) cena also means she has dinner.
Pan dulce: Mexican sweet bread.
¿Puede repetir, por favor?
